entries.text: The raft is suspended, not bolted to the belly. A hard-mounted gondola feeds its thrust and slosh moments straight into film-on-rings, and the 4 mm wall has no line for that local bending. Pendants on a wide bridle arrive nearly tangential, so the wall sees distributed pulls along straps that ride many rings in bearing. The hull is huge, so the bridle can be wide and the swing angle small. The price is a pendulum in the control loop, and ops owns it. Both readings are [SCOPING]. The equipment axis is scoped rather than weighed in the gated ledger; Mission 0 carries it as a spec figure: 19 t of gear against 100 t of water at 112 m.
entries.reason: The scoped raft paragraph gives equipment and water masses, plus wall dimensions; it makes no structural float result.

entries.text: Mission 0 wears this same fit. Mission 0 is a scoping scenario, distinct from the hull of record. It uses this architecture at 112 m, with 100 t of water and 19 t of equipment. Its mid-band structural mass is a target with unverified inputs and unpriced shear hardware, not a drawn floating vehicle. The 52 m hull comes first; Mission 0 is its next configuration. The hull below carries the whole verdict.

entries.text: Bracing pays twice. Bending falls as the cube of the bracing pitch, so spokes buy strength cheaply — and they buy back volume. Every panel dimples inward and that dent is open to the sky, so an unbraced cell forfeits [data-n="edge.bulgeVolumeLostUnbracedPct" data-f="1"] % of its own displacement. Spoked and solved over every real panel, the pumped-down article gives up [data-n="skin.loadedDishPct" data-f="1"] % — the ledger carries it. On anything meant to float, that is a fifth of the lift.

entries.text: It is a membrane, not a barrier. The [data-n="skin.hexArealGM2" data-f="2"] g/m² above is sized for strength . A real barrier laminate of the class this project has measured is several times heavier, and wrapped around a cell this size that is lift-negative on its own skin — deliberately, because the demonstrator is not meant to be flight representative. Only a deposited stack scales to every cell size, and nobody has a measured number for one on printed PAHT-CF. That is the barrier-stack experiment, and it must be measured rather than argued. The arithmetic behind that comparison lives in research/notes/barrier-and-permeation.md , marked as arithmetic and under no checker, so this page does not put a figure on it.

entries.text: Everything that is not lift hangs outside the vacuum, on a pipe-frame raft slung under the keel from a wide bridle: water tanks, nitrogen ballast, generators, batteries, the cryo plant, and the ship's mind. The working lines drop from the raft, and they are colour-coded by job — pink carries weight (the bucket line, the bridle), blue carries water (the pump's rigid pipe, the sprayer feed). The top half of the hull is decked in solar panels; the rotors sit on pylons on the horizontal beam of the ship, as far from lines and film as the geometry allows, because their hardest work is pushing up — holding the buoyant hull down against a lake while the pump drinks.
entries.reason: The gear layout describes the simulated filling cycle; its buoyant-hull assumption is explicitly separated from structural evidence.
